title: Nitrogen and hydrogen A
hook: Count the particles and find what runs out.

knows: A balanced equation gives ratios of reactant and product particles.
doesNotKnow: How unequal starting amounts determine a limiting reactant.

misconception: The reactant with the smaller raw count is always limiting.
objective: Find the limiting reactant from a balanced equation and stated starting counts.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: In the particle model N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃, start with 2 N₂ and 3 H₂ molecules. If complete reaction is possible, which reactant limits the products? The equation permits 1 complete reaction set in this particle model. It forms 2 NH₃ and leaves 1 N₂ and 0 H₂. H₂ is the limiting reactant. Atom totals are conserved.
claims.source: Specified particle counts and balanced equation; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/4-4-reaction-yields

claims.text: The circles are atoms grouped for counting; shapes and trajectories are schematic, not molecular geometry or a reaction mechanism.
Recall: For 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O, if 4 H₂ and 1 O₂ react completely, which limits the product? One O₂ uses two H₂, so O₂ runs out with two H₂ left over.

recall.question: For 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O, if 4 H₂ and 1 O₂ react completely, which limits the product?
recall.why: One O₂ uses two H₂, so O₂ runs out with two H₂ left over.
